The test image shows a field of tomato plants with apparent wilting/stress symptoms visible across multiple rows — characteristic of a systemic disease. Plants appear wilted, some drooping, with the damage spread throughout the field. This points toward bacterial wilt or vascular disease candidates.

Now I'll view one reference from each of 8 different classes.

The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood_4.jpg) has image ID **1568041** — the test image ID is **1568048**, consecutive numbers from the same Bugwood series. This is a strong signal they're from the same disease set.

I've now used all 8 reference image views. Let me summarize my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Field-level view of tomato plants in rows
- Plants showing wilting/drooping, some appear collapsed
- Pattern of partial field collapse consistent with bacterial wilt spread
- Bugwood image ID: **1568048**

**Key finding:** The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference Bugwood_4.jpg carries Bugwood ID **1568041** — only 7 apart from the test image ID 1568048. Both are from the same Bugwood submission series, strongly suggesting they document the same disease.

**Reference comparison:**
- Bacterial_Wilt references: all showed stem bacterial streaming tests (lab diagnostic) — no field view match
- Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (Bugwood_14): showed collapsed, wilted tomato plant — matches the field wilting pattern
- Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (Bugwood_4, ID 1568041): vascular browning cross-section from same series as test image
- Verticillium_Wilt: showed leaf-level yellowing/wilting symptoms
- Phytophthora_Blight: showed stem collapse/blackening at ground level
- Southern_Blight: showed white mycelium at stem base

The field-level wilting pattern in the test image, combined with the Bugwood ID proximity to the Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference series (1568041 → 1568048), points clearly to Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.
